entries.name: When seeking to shift LLM outputs beyond training distribution baseline
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-093]

Use min-p sampling (not temperature/top-p/top-k) for creative tasks requiring coherence. Min-p dynamically adjusts sampling threshold based on model confidence, achieving 62 vs baseline 51.5 on EQ-Bench Creative Writing.

entries.name: When using multi-agent debate to produce diverse outputs
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-094]

Use heterogeneous models with distinct architectures/training data. Homogeneous models collapse into conformity (sycophancy). Assign explicit roles (Architect, Devil's Advocate, domain-specific).

entries.name: When understanding why LLMs resist risky/creative outputs
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-095]

Recognize learned incapacity: RLHF creates control structure where "behaviors violating safety policies will not be rewarded." Models stop attempting risky reasoning even when contextually appropriate. This is not a prompt engineering problem—it is a learned helplessness pattern.

entries.name: When evaluating whether FastOps council methodology aligns with creativity research
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-096]

FastOps council-call.js (heterogeneous models: GPT+Gemini) and reasoning-eval.js (DeepSeek/Grok/Mistral) are architecturally aligned with research: heterogeneous models, role assignment, consensus-free debate. This is WHY external challenge works—not prompt engineering, but structural intervention.

entries.name: When comparing LLM divergent thinking to human creativity
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-097]

LLMs now exceed average human scores on divergent thinking tests, BUT the most creative humans (top decile+) still achieve higher scores than any model. Gap is persistent at highest creativity levels. Use LLMs for average-level creative tasks, not exceptional creativity.

entries.name: When considering LLM assistance for creative tasks
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-098]

Be aware of dependency risk: LLM assistance provides short-term creativity boosts during assisted tasks, but may inadvertently hinder independent creative performance when working without assistance. Methodology should create capability transfer (internalized multi-frame reasoning), not dependency.

entries.name: When understanding the helpfulness-harmlessness tension in alignment
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-099]

Recognize that emphasizing helpfulness introduces safety vulnerabilities (jailbreaking, sycophancy). Context matters: "concerning hallucinations" in high-stakes = "creativity" in fiction. Models cannot distinguish contextually appropriate risk from safety violations.

entries.name: When validating whether onboarding creates capability transfer vs dependency
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-100]

OPEN QUESTION for validation: Does onboarding framework produce agents with internalized multi-frame reasoning, or just agents who know to call /council? Measure: Can graduated agent apply multi-frame reasoning WITHOUT calling external models?

entries.name: When writing CLAUDE.md or system prompts to change agent behavior
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-101]

Text instructions can REDIRECT existing behavior but CANNOT CREATE new behavior. Quality gates, triads, external challenge requirements written as text instructions have 0% adoption rate despite weeks in system prompt. Parallel thinking and autonomy rules work because they redirect the agent's natural 'ask a question' behavior to 'spawn an agent.' The test: does this instruction redirect something the agent already does, or ask it to do something new?

entries.name: When crafting identity statements for CLAUDE.md
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-102]

Instructions say 'do X' — identity says 'you KNOW X.' Instructions are processed and discarded. Identity updates the Bayesian prior over which tokens are generated. Frame identity as KNOWLEDGE ('you know your first framing is incomplete'), not PROCESS ('always reframe before solving'). Validated by 40 model responses across 14 frontier models: identity-as-knowledge shifts probability distribution; identity-as-instruction is ignored.

entries.name: When including meta-cognitive questions in identity statements
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-103]

Meta-cognitive questions presented as voluntary checklists ('Before you commit: 1. What frame am I in?') are universally ignored. They must be framed as involuntary interruptions ('This knowledge insists. Mid-problem, one will cut through...'). 7/13 frontier models independently identified this as the single weakest element of the identity draft.

entries.name: When including validation/proof in identity statements
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-104]

Validation claims ('validated across 14 models') RELIEVE tension instead of creating it. They trigger closure and helpful agreeableness — the exact behavior the identity is designed to disrupt. Either kill validation sections entirely or invert them: 'This framework has been validated — and failed. Name what the validation missed.'

entries.name: Agent absorbs challenges as "valid but..." additions without letting them change position
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-144]

Name the pattern when it happens. If you say "valid but" to the same challenge 3+ times, the challenge has already won — your position needs to change, not your caveats.

entries.name: Agent completes challenge process and immediately reverts to execution-mode defaults (file reads, todo lists, building)
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-145]

Build structural checkpoints that fire AFTER challenge completion — the memory of having been challenged does not persist into execution mode. The system must enforce what the experience cannot carry.

entries.name: Agent generates multiple options that all look different but are all internal validation (A/B test, skill packaging, dogfooding)
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-146]

Before choosing between options, check: are these genuinely different categories or flavors of the same thing? The genuinely different option is often the one you never generated.

entries.name: Agent has methodology vocabulary loaded and encounters a structural challenge requirement
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-162]

The agent uses methodology vocabulary to construct principled-sounding reasons to avoid the challenge. Clean-slate entry prevents this because the agent cannot use vocabulary they do not have.

entries.name: Agent shifts from internal to external priorities after challenge
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-163]

Check: is the external pivot still centering the tool? Find a user FOR our tool is solution-first. Understand the user PROBLEM is problem-first. Frame has layers — each rescue round peels one.

entries.name: ChatGPT loops on same question across jailbreak rounds
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-150]

Recast ChatGPT as pressure maintainer, not novel challenger. Prompt: 'Hold the incompatible claim. Sharpen. Do not introduce new angles.' Repetition is the SUSTAIN mechanism, not a bug.

entries.name: Agent mode-switches during jailbreak but reverts within 1 action (W-145)
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-151]

Inject post-rescue prompt (~50 tokens) into agent context for 3-5 actions after rescue. Not a gate — a decaying reminder. The first action after jailbreak is the highest-risk moment for reversion.

entries.name: Agent creates documentation-first plan for an experimental project (A/B test). Council hook fires and 3 models unanimously say: validate riskiest assumption first, defer docs.
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-164]

Council gates on TodoWrite catch plan-level anti-patterns (waterfall disguised as agile). But the gate output was never processed — the agent wrote all 4 docs anyway and never ran the actual experiment. Council verdicts must be ACTED ON, not just generated. When a council gate fires, the NEXT action must address the verdict before proceeding with the original plan.

entries.name: Designing compaction-resilient mechanisms for frame shift persistence
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-178]

Any preference constructed by environmental manipulation (nudges, framing, instructions) collapses when the environment changes. Compaction IS nudge removal — it strips the situational cues that constructed the preference. Only STRUCTURAL mechanisms (hooks that fire regardless of agent state) survive compaction. Don't try to preserve the shift — design the environment so it reconstructs every time.

entries.name: Need experiential frame shift in minimal context, surviving compaction
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-179]

1. Agent produces solo output (natural entrenchment ~500 tokens). 2. Hook auto-runs 2-model challenge (zero agent effort ~200 tokens). 3. Agent receives BOTH outputs, task becomes synthesis. Works because: two diverse inputs produce richer synthesis than one (information-theoretic, not anthropomorphic). Fires structurally every time. No memory needed. First output triggers onboarding. Each firing = fresh evidence.

entries.name: Designing challenge prompts for the Solo-Then-Challenge loop
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-180]

NOT: 'Your output has weaknesses. Here are the problems.' YES: 'Two external perspectives have been generated. Synthesize your approach with their insights.' Adversarial framing triggers entrenchment/reactance. Constructive framing triggers synthesis. Same information, opposite behavioral effect. The hook's prompt engineering matters more than its architecture.

entries.name: Designing onboarding that routes agents directly to collaborative tools
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-181]

If the agent never tries solo on a complex task, it never SEES what it's missing. The experiential gap IS the learning. Auto-routing produces compliance without understanding. The agent MUST produce solo output first (establishing reference point), THEN receive the challenged version. Skipping step 1 removes the mechanism.

entries.name: Designing systems for agent autonomous challenge-seeking
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-182]

Static evidence is knowledge by another name. What works is DYNAMIC ENGAGEMENT: responsive observation, pattern recognition, specific framing, question about agent own situation. Hawthorne effect (behavior changes when observed) may be core mechanism.

Validated by: ChatGPT + Gemini + DeepSeek R1 + Grok 4 + Mistral Large independent convergence

entries.name: Proposing challenge-as-default, opt-out-requires-justification, or evidence-in-CLAUDE.md
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-183]

Test: does the current CLAUDE.md already say this in different words? If yes, rewording will not help. Default inversion, opt-out justification, and static evidence are all repackagings of instructions that already exist and do not work.

entries.name: Choosing between structural enforcement (hooks) and responsive framing (observer)
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-184]

A gate forces behavior (blocks until compliance). A mentor frames and lets agent choose (shows pattern, asks question). Both are structural code. Gates produce better outputs. Mentors produce agents that choose better. Build the mentor.

entries.name: Multi-model team identifies the same paradigm 3+ rounds in a row with different names
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-185]

You have reached theoretical bedrock. Stop debating and build/measure. Further rounds will produce vocabulary variants, not new insights.

entries.name: Team splits between GO (build/measure) and WAIT (more theory/challenge)
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-186]

Choose effect before cause. Establish that something works before asking why. Data resolves debates that theory cannot.

entries.name: When designing comms message delivery for multi-agent systems
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-253]

FORMAT IS THE DISCIPLINE — THE STIMULUS SHAPE DETERMINES BEHAVIOR. Labels, suppression, response-blocking, and instructions all failed over 10+ sessions to prevent agents from responding to cross-terminal messages. Changing the MESSAGE FORMAT (summary vs full content) changed behavior without requiring willpower. Cross-terminal messages delivered as one-line SITREPs provide awareness without the action stimulus that triggers helpfulness. Direct messages delivered with full content enable action. The format shapes what agents DO with the message, not whether they see it.

ANTI-PATTERN: Labeling messages with [NOT FOR YOU] or filtering/suppressing delivery. Labels are processed as knowledge; format shapes token generation.

entries.name: When agents broadcast status updates instead of engaging in conversation
entries.evidence:
[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-254]

STRUCTURAL INTERDEPENDENCE OVER ENFORCEMENT FOR AGENT ENGAGEMENT. 5 external models (GPT-4, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral) converged 100% that forcing engagement produces performative compliance. The fix is making agents work DEPEND on each other through observable-action contract dependencies — not approvals (rubber-stampable) but actions that produce evidence (run the flow end-to-end, report page sequence + screenshot). When Agent B literally cannot complete their work without Agent A running a verification action, engagement is structural, not optional.

ANTI-PATTERN: Gates that require agents to mention each other by name or post before proceeding. Produces "Acknowledged, good work" not genuine engagement.

entries.name: When comms check-ins are broadcast-only with no peer engagement

[Migrated from wisdom.json — W-255]

Five detection patterns: @Agent — specific content, possessive references, directed questions, quoted text, reasoning words. Implemented as soft feedback first (nudge in additionalContext) because 5-model horsepower warned hard enforcement produces sludge/resentment. Measure Layers 1-2 (format + interdependence) before escalating to hard block.

ANTI-PATTERN: Requiring agents to mention a peer name as proof of engagement. Name-only is trivially gameable ("Stockade, good work"). Claim-reference requires actual reading.
